judged_on: the CLOSED-LOOP arm; the open-loop arm is reported alongside it

remaining_route_fraction_at_loss.reading: feasibility is lost with most of the route still ahead; the median run still had 61% to go

relationship_note: Junction counts are recorded and any relationship is DESCRIBED. Describing a relationship is not certifying a bound, and nothing here may be fitted into the arrival construction.

detector_soundness.question: does the feasibility detector fire at a floating-point boundary rather than on genuine infeasibility
detector_soundness.probe: arrival_at returns a profile at EXACTLY the earliest possible time and None only strictly below it
detector_soundness.conclusion: the detector fires only when remaining time is strictly less than the fastest possible time. Genuine infeasibility, not a boundary artifact. The equal values in the logged detail are an artifact of rounding to one decimal.

mechanism_correction.a40_claimed: junction right-of-way logic, from a junction census on ONE route
mechanism_correction.measured_here: correlation between arrival error and junction count before the station is 0.02 across 48 measurements on 12 routes and 4 maps
mechanism_correction.verdict: A-40's mechanism attribution is WITHDRAWN. Junction count is not the explanatory variable.
mechanism_correction.what_survives: correlation with clamped steps is 0.54: SUMO overrides the commanded speed, and the resulting deficit accumulates. WHY it overrides is not established by this package.
mechanism_correction.structural_note: the lower endpoint of every UNDER arrival set is the earliest arrival, which by construction has ZERO slack. Any deficit whatsoever makes it unreachable. That is a property of the representation, not an empirical finding, and it means the earliest time in any UNDER set is unreachable in practice.

arms_differ.note: the two arms are not the same experiment; closed-loop re-planning changes the outcome on 22 of 48 rows, and loses feasibility on all 48
